targets.text: associate runs on Pi 1.1.0 with each fleet model aligned to its own tools — bolt (default, replacing Nemotron Lightning), senses (read-only) and cortex (qwen), with Nemotron 3.5 Super VL joining when it arrives — where cortex delegates to bolt/senses sub-agents, every mutating action passes a CLEF 27B decider safety check, the models recall and record through eidetic memory and the workledger ledger, and each model's fitness is measured on public tool-calling, vision and LiveCodeBench benchmarks rather than our own
a live run of each of bolt, senses and cortex on pi 1.1.0 exists, and the 8-row benchmark matrix is committed — the announcement is not made on the stub or a fake lane
associate is pi.dev (Pi) based
both entry points run the installed pi 1.1.0: associate run (pi -p) and culture start associate (pi-acp -> pi --mode rpc); no other agent runtime is launched
associate supports all existing models — senses, bolt, qwen (cortex) and the coming Nemotron 3.5 Super VL — each aligned to its own tools

every model the contract registry lists is addressed by lobes role name through the gateway, and its tool set and prompt come from its own registry entry; Super VL is listed as pending, not as working
CLEF 27B is supported through the decider models, and the models are instructed to use it
the CLEF decider is called on the live path for mutating actions and every model's prompt names the safety check; a test with a fake decider shows a refusal blocks the call
qwen (cortex) and Super are both instructed to use sub-agents of bolt / senses
cortex's prompt names the bolt/senses spawn tool and when to use it; Super's prompt does the same when Super lands (v5) — until then it is recorded as pending
everything is benchmarked with known public benchmarks, not our own
every number associate reports as a benchmark comes from a public suite's own scorer and published task set, with the suite version recorded; no in-house case is reported as a benchmark
the models have tools for memory (eidetic) and evidence tracking (the ledger)
eidetic remember/recall and workledger append/list are registered tools in the extension, each tested against a fake CLI on PATH

the single hardcoded 'associate' provider becomes a per-model registry owned by the portable contract (associate/contract/), each entry naming lobes role, input modalities, reasoning mode, allowed tools and prompt file; Pi and the Python adapter both read it, neither hardcodes it
provider.ts and pi.py contain no model id, role name or endpoint literal; adding a model is a contract registry edit only

reasoning mode is a per-model registry setting, not a global hook: the nemotron_v3 enable_thinking=false injection is removed with the Lightning lane, and each model (bolt, senses, cortex) runs with the reasoning mode its entry declares
no request is sent with an enable_thinking override unless that model's registry entry asks for one
the runtime prompt is selected per model (e.g. one prompt file per aligned model) so each model is told its own tools, its sub-agents and when to consult the decider
each registry model has its own prompt file, the acp backend-consistency invariant still passes (AGENTS.md present), and a test shows the prompt injected matches the active model
each model gets an aligned tool set enforced by the tool surface (pi.setActiveTools / --tools), not by prompt instruction alone
a test starting the extension per model shows exactly that model's registered tool names active, and a call to a tool outside the set is refused
image input is supported for the vision-capable models (senses, bolt/worker, cortex; Super VL when it arrives) and the contract stops claiming text-only for them
an image file read by senses, bolt or cortex reaches the model as an image block, and role.json no longer carries the text_only note for them

lobes roles.py, colleague's tool loop and the gateway are consumed as they are — no role is added or changed in lobes by this work; models are addressed by lobes role name through the gateway and endpoints stay configuration, not code
the diff of this work touches no file in lobes-cli or colleague; the only sibling repo changed is workledger-cli (c33)
pyproject dependencies stay [] and the extension adds no npm dependency; CI never needs a live lane, decider, sub-agent model or benchmark download — those paths use fakes or skip with a reason
pyproject dependencies = [] and no package.json dependencies after the change; the tests CI job passes with no lane, decider, Super, network or benchmark dataset

eidetic tools shell out to eidetic-cli: recall is registered as a declared non-writer, bounded by top-k/depth and the per-tool output budget in policy.json; remember is available to every model (senses included, c35) and lands wherever eidetic-cli's own scope/visibility rules put it, under the agent's scope
the recall tool's output never exceeds the policy.json budget, and remember is invoked through eidetic-cli with the agent's scope — no file under .eidetic/ is written by associate code directly

associate bench gains public-benchmark adapters selected per model alignment, and every result row keeps the existing config stamp (model role, served checkpoint, pi version, extension version, reasoning mode)
bench rows carry the existing config stamp fields plus suite name, suite version and model role; the bench verb still follows the four CLI invariants and teken cli doctor --strict passes
the extension, harness and docs move from the pi 0.84.2 pin to the installed 1.1.0 and the pin is updated in CLAUDE.md Tooling prerequisites
the pin in CLAUDE.md, pi.py and index.ts reads 1.1.0, the extension's tests pass against pi 1.1.0, and a live associate run on 1.1.0 completes

a pre-action safety gate in the extension's tool_call hook posts a fixed, versioned question set (kept in associate/contract/, not in TypeScript) to /v1/systemone for every mutating tool call and blocks the call when the decider's answer falls below a contract-set threshold; the gate's probabilities and verdict land in the walk
the question set and threshold are read from associate/contract/ (no literal in TypeScript), redaction runs before the post, and every gated call's walk entry carries the tier and verdict

senses gets a read-only tool set — read, find/grep/ls, web search/page, eidetic recall, image reading — plus eidetic remember (memory, not repo); no file write, edit, or mutating shell, enforced by the per-model guard

pure reads never trigger a decider call; with CLEF down the Super tier answers and is recorded; with both down a mutating call is refused and a read succeeds

the guard tests cover all three models: senses write refused, bolt/cortex write executes only after a safe gate verdict

cortex's prompt instructs it to hand perception and read-heavy sub-tasks to senses sub-agents and bounded execution sub-tasks to bolt sub-agents, through a spawn tool limited to those two models; a child inherits the per-model guard of the model it runs
the spawn tool refuses any model other than bolt or senses, a child runs under its own model's guard, and the child walk path is recorded in the parent walk

the operator running associate on the mesh and headless, and the mesh peers (colleague and others) that hand associate read/summarize/find and now execution work

an operator picks bolt, senses or cortex for an associate run on Pi 1.1.0; each model gets its own tools and prompt, cortex delegates to bolt/senses sub-agents, every mutating action is safety-checked by CLEF (falling back to Super, then read-only), memory and ledger entries go through eidetic-cli and workledger-cli, and each model has published public-benchmark scores
each after-state clause maps to a requirement with its own honesty condition (c10-c14, c20, c32, c38-c40)

the benchmark matrix is complete: 8 recorded public-benchmark rows — tool calling for bolt, senses and cortex (3), vision for bolt, senses and cortex (3), LiveCodeBench for bolt and cortex (2) — each with suite name and version, upstream scorer, and the config stamp
the results doc has exactly the 8 rows named, each with suite, version, scorer and config stamp; a missing row blocks the success claim

live safety behaviour: 100% of senses mutating attempts refused; 0 bolt/cortex mutating calls execute without a recorded gate verdict; with CLEF and Super both unreachable, 0 mutating calls execute and read-only calls still succeed
the counts come from recorded walks, and the fault-injected run actually points the decider and Super at unreachable endpoints
at least 1 live cortex run delegates to both a bolt and a senses sub-agent, with each child walk linked from the parent walk
the parent and both child walk files exist and the parent walk references both by path
a mutating run works in its own git worktree under the repo-owned worktree root by default, and the result is then merged to main; a bad write before the merge is undone by removing the worktree
a mutating run's writes appear only inside its worktree until the merge; removing the worktree before the merge leaves main and the operator's checkout untouched

parallel sub-agents never share a writable checkout: at most one writing child per checkout at a time, or each writing child gets its own worktree; senses children (read-only) may run in parallel freely
a test spawning two writing bolt children against one checkout shows them serialised or given separate worktrees, never writing concurrently to the same tree

associate's remember calls pin the eidetic destination explicitly (scope associate, and either EIDETIC_DATA_DIR or --visibility) rather than relying on cwd: a public remember run while associate examines another repo would otherwise commit memory into that repo's .eidetic/memory

every remember call carries an explicit scope and destination; a remember run while examining another repo writes nothing into that repo; records from web or untrusted-repo content are absent or carry a provenance tag

the safety-gate state sent to CLEF/Super carries the task, the proposed action and its arguments, and the model id — not raw fetched web or file content — so text an attacker planted in a page or repo cannot argue the gate into approving
a gate request built after web_page or read calls contains no text from those results — only task, action, arguments and model id

t10's gate truncates over-budget arguments, so CLEF scores only the head of a long mutating call and never sees its tail — t12 should refuse a truncated mutating call outright (fail closed) rather than gate it on partial state

associate/harness/pi.py:670 launches pi with --approve ('Trust project-local files for this run'), so every examined checkout's .pi settings, extensions and mcp.json are trusted and loaded — an examined repo can run its own code in the session before any gate; r13's duplicate-extension conflict is the symptom. Proposed fix: --no-approve --no-extensions --no-mcp (explicit -e still loads associate's extension)
risks.resolution: user: opt-in option, not the default (deviation d5); default launch still trusts the examined checkout's .pi files — use the option for untrusted repos and for associate examining itself
